evidence.excerpt:
private[ember] def postProcessResponse[F[_]](
      req: Request[F],
      resp: Response[F],
      drain: F[Option[Array[Byte]]],
      nextBytes: Ref[F, Array[Byte]],
      canBeReused: Ref[F, Reusable])(implicit F: Concurrent[F]): F[Unit] =
    drain.flatMap {
      case Some(bytes) =>
        val requestClose = req.headers.get(Connection).exists(_.hasClose)
        val responseClose = resp.headers.get(Connection).exists(_.hasClose)

        if (requestClose || responseClose) F.unit
        else nextBytes.set(bytes) >> canBeReused.set(Reusable.Reuse)
      case None => F.unit
    }
evidence.interpretation: Source observation: only Some(bytes), absent close headers, saves remainder and marks reuse; None leaves the default non-reusable state unchanged.

claims.rule: For HEAD/no-body response parsing, review exposed body, buffered remainder, unread socket bytes and connection reuse separately; an empty drain marker alone must not be presented as consumed network data.
claims.applicability: Inference from a 2024 HTTP/1 Ember response-parser review. Reviewer-reported connection closure explains disposition, but future pooling changes require fresh connection-level tests. A HEAD Content-Length need not imply body bytes to read.
claims.counterexample: Do not blindly read Content-Length bytes from a valid HEAD response: they may never arrive. This is not a request-parser rule, an HTTP/2 framing prescription, or a mandate to discard every status-related remainder.

claims.rule: When refactoring Ember response cleanup, preserve the distinction between incomplete None and completed Some(empty), save next-message remainder before allowing reuse, and release at response Resource scope even when no body is consumed.
claims.applicability: Derived from the adopted CE2 series/0.21 body-draining revision and checked against the later CE3 HEAD consumer. Socket draining and exhaustive chunking were explicitly deferred; current reuse changes need fresh owner-level tests.
claims.counterexample: A completely consumed response with no already-buffered next response is not incomplete. Do not replace Some(empty) with None or insist on reading arbitrarily large unwanted bodies before releasing a connection.
